title: Safety Tax in Reasoning Models: Does RLHF Safety Training Degrade Mathematical Reasoning Proportionally Across Problem Difficulty?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: if safety training preferentially degrades hard reasoning, it sharpens the safety-capability trade-off. However, the link to actionable safety improvement has a gap since it characterizes a problem without suggesting a fix.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Comparing model performance on math benchmarks at different difficulty levels is straightforward evaluation work. Requires API access to reasoning models and running standard benchmarks. Intermediate but feasible with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: accuracy gap vs. difficulty level plot. Uses existing benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH) with established difficulty ratings. One comparison pair suffices. Fits in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is largely addressed by existing work. 'Safety Tax: Safety Alignment Makes Your Large Reasoning Models Less Reasonable' (Huang et al., arXiv:2503.00555, March 2025) directly studies the degradation of reasoning capability from safety alignment in large reasoning models. Follow-up work includes 'Mitigating the Safety Alignment Tax with Null-Space Constrained Policy Optimization' (arXiv:2512.11391) and 'LoRA is All You Need for Safety Alignment of Reasoning LLMs' (arXiv:2507.17075). The specific difficulty-stratified analysis (whether degradation is proportional across problem difficulty levels) is a minor extension of the existing 'Safety Tax' paper's findings, not a substantially novel contribution.
